name: Amelia Island Museum of History
content: Housed inside a former jail in Fernandina Beach, this site serves as the starting hub for dark history and ghost tours detailing tales of pirates, bootleggers, and restless spirits of historic Amelia Island.

name: Apollo I Launch Complex 34
content: Located at Launch Complex 34 on Cape Canaveral, this was the site of the fatal 1967 fire for the Apollo 1 mission. Since then visitors have reported eerie sounds and the sense of a lingering presence off the pad.

name: Ashley's Restaurant
content: Located in Rockledge, Florida, this historic landmark and former 1930s tavern is famous for paranormal activity—most notably attributed to the spirit of Ethel Allen, alongside flickering lights and moving glassware.

name: Athens Theatre
content: This restored 1920s theatre in DeLand is said to host lingering spirits, including a former stagehand who fell to his death and a spirited young actress who frequents the balcony.

name: Bellamy Bridge
content: The historic Bellamy Bridge in Jackson County (built circa 1914) is known as “Florida’s most haunted bridge.” Legend holds that a bride who died tragically still wanders the swamp near the span on moonlit nights.

name: Biltmore Hotel
content: The Biltmore Hotel in Coral Gables (opened 1926) once served as a luxury resort and later a military hospital. A mobster murdered on the 13th floor is said to haunt the hotel’s historic corridors.

name: Blue Anchor Pub
content: The Blue Anchor Pub in Delray Beach (originally an 1840s London pub moved to Florida) is said to be haunted by “Bertha Starkey” who appears around 10 p.m., rattling pots and moaning in the kitchen.

name: Bosque Bello Cemetery
content: Established in Fernandina Beach in the late 1700s, this moss-draped cemetery is renowned for spectral sightings, ghostly giggles, and reports of children lingering among its historic headstones.

name: Bulow Plantation Ruins Historic State Park
content: Hidden deep in Flagler County, the coquina ruins of this 1800s sugar mill destroyed during the Second Seminole War are home to reports of mysterious cold spots, shadowy figures, and glowing orbs.

name: Captain Tony's Saloon
content: Built over an old 19th-century morgue around a historic hanging tree in Key West, this iconic bar is famous for unexplained encounters, lingering spirits like the 'Lady in Blue', and disembodied voices.

name: Cassadaga Cemetery
content: Within the spiritualist community of Cassadaga, the cemetery’s “Devil’s Chair” bench invites mischief — leave a beer and sit and legend says a dark spirit might emerge.

name: Castillo de San Marcos
content: The 17th-century Spanish fort in St. Augustine, Florida — the oldest masonry fort in the continental US — has tales of phantom muskets, unseen footsteps in the turrets, and a sense of soldiers still on guard.

name: Cuban Club
content: The Cuban Club in Tampa’s Ybor City is one of America’s most haunted buildings — reports include a drowned child in the basement pool, ballroom balcony ghosts, and hundreds of unseen presences.

name: DeBary Hall Historic Site
content: Constructed in 1871 along the St. Johns River as a hunting retreat, this 8,000-square-foot historic mansion is known for persistent reports of paranormal phenomena, footsteps, and unexplained activity.

name: Deering Estate
content: Overlooking Biscayne Bay in Miami, this historic 444-acre coastal preserve is widely regarded as one of Miami's most active paranormal sites, featuring ghosts of early settlers and indigenous spirits.

name: Devil’s Tree
content: Located near New Smyrna Beach, this lone tree is an old oak said to house the ghost of an executed man; local legend warns visitors of ominous feelings and strange lights.

name: Edison & Ford Winter Estates
content: Located along the Caloosahatchee River in Fort Myers, visitors and staff at this historic riverside estate have reported ghostly apparitions of Thomas Edison and Henry Ford roaming the grounds and laboratory.

name: Ernest Hemingway Home & Museum
content: Beyond its famous polydactyl cats, this Key West estate is said to be haunted by Hemingway himself, with reports of his spectral image waving from the balcony or writing in his upper-loft office.

name: Florida Theatre
content: Opening in Downtown Jacksonville in 1927, this grand Mediterranean Revival theater is famous for a phantom figure seen in the upper balcony and mysterious light anomalies captured on security cameras.

name: Fort Clinch State Park
content: Located on Amelia Island, this Civil War-era brick fortress is reputedly haunted by Confederate and Union soldiers. Ghostly sightings include a soldier pacing the ramparts at night.

name: Fort Pickens
content: Situated on Pensacola's Santa Rosa Island, this 1830s military fort held Apache chief Geronimo as a prisoner. Visitors report disembodied footsteps, cold spots, and shadowy figures in the brick tunnels.

name: Gilbert’s Bar House of Refuge
content: On Hutchinson Island near Stuart, Florida, this 19th-century shipwreck survivor station turned refuge is said to be haunted by castaways and lost mariners whose voices echo through the old building.

name: Greenwood Cemetery
content: Spanning over 100 acres in Orlando, this historic burial ground established in 1880 features nighttime ghost tours highlighting restless spirits, cold spots, and unexplained occurrences among old mausoleums.

name: Henry B. Plant Museum / Former Tampa Bay Hotel
content: Located on the University of Tampa campus, this 1891 Victorian railroad resort features reports of a ghost known as the 'Brown Lady,' unexplained organ music, and moving artifacts.

name: Historic Cocoa Village Playhouse
content: Operating since 1924, this Brevard County theater is reputed to have a resident ghost named 'Joe' who tinkers with stage lights and projection equipment after midnight.

name: Huguenot Cemetery
content: Established outside St. Augustine's city gates during the 1821 yellow fever epidemic, this burial ground is famous for the ghost of Judge John B. Stickney, seen wandering in search of his stolen gold teeth.

name: Island Hotel
content: The Island Hotel in Cedar Key, Florida (built in the late 1800s) has rumored hauntings: footsteps in vacant rooms, doors opening on their own, and a guest who awoke to a figure beside the bed.

name: Key West Cemetery
content: The historic Key West Cemetery is known for its “graveyard jokes” and for spirits said to wander among the headstones — visitors report cold spots, whispering, and the sense of being watched.

name: Kingsley Plantation
content: Located on Fort George Island in Jacksonville, this 19th-century estate harbors tales of shadowy figures near the tabby slave quarters and lingering spirits within the plantation house.

name: Koreshan State Park
content: In the grounds of this former theocratic community near Estero, Florida, visitors report ghostly figures in vintage dress and unexplained footsteps inside the old settlement’s buildings.

name: Lakeside Inn
content: Operating since 1883 in Mount Dora, Florida's oldest continuously operating hotel is known for ghostly children running down hallways and spectral figures lingering in the historic lobby.

name: Lightner Museum / Former Hotel Alcazar
content: Built by Henry Flagler in 1888 in St. Augustine, this Gilded Age landmark is home to reports of mysterious voices near the old indoor pool area and apparitions in antique exhibit halls.

name: Ma Barker House
content: The house in Ocklawaha where outlaw gang leader Ma Barker and her son Fred reportedly took refuge — folklore holds the house is haunted by their violent history and shadowy figures seen at dusk.

name: May-Stringer House
content: The May-Stringer House (Brooksville, Florida) is often called “Florida’s most haunted house.” Reports include the ghost of a child, cold spots, orbs of light, and whispers in the attic.

name: Old City Cemetery
content: Established in 1829 in Tallahassee, this historic resting place contains graves of Yellow Fever victims and Civil War soldiers, with frequent reports of spectral figures and strange lights.

name: Orman House Historic State Park
content: Built in 1838 along Apalachicola Bay by cotton merchant Thomas Orman, visitors to this antebellum home report creaking floorboards, disembodied footsteps, and feeling watched in the upstairs rooms.

name: Richey Suncoast Theatre
content: Originally built as a movie palace in 1925 in New Port Richey, theater staff and performers have long reported cold spots, phantom footsteps, and a spectral gentleman watching rehearsals from the seats.

name: Robert the Doll
content: Housed in Key West, the infamous Robert the Doll is said to move on his own, giggle, and bring misfortune if disrespected. Visitors tell chilling tales of photos failing and strange feelings.

name: Saenger Theatre
content: Opening in Pensacola in 1925, this historic venue features stories of a friendly ghost nicknamed 'Paul' who assists stage crews and moves theater equipment when the building is quiet.

name: Sarasota Opera House
content: First opened as the Edwards Theatre in 1926, performers and staff report an unseen presence in the basement dressing rooms and mysterious shadows passing behind the stage curtains.

name: St. Augustine Lighthouse
content: On Anastasia Island, the St. Augustine Lighthouse and keeper’s house are reputedly haunted by drowned children and a former keeper — shadowy figures and strange voices have been reported.

name: St. Francis Inn
content: Dating back to 1791 in St. Augustine, Florida's oldest inn is famous for the tragic ghost of 'Lily', a young servant whose spirit moves objects, turns on faucets, and visits guests in room 2B.

name: St. Michael's Cemetery
content: Spanning eight acres in Pensacola, this 18th-century Spanish colonial burial ground is renowned for sightings of ghostly apparitions in period dress and mysterious glowing orbs near historic vaults.

name: Stranahan House
content: The oldest surviving structure in Fort Lauderdale, the Stranahan House is said to host the spirit of Annie Stranahan, whose kitchen ghostly figure has been seen by visitors and staff.

name: Sunshine Skyway Bridge
content: Spanning Tampa Bay, the bridge is linked to tragic collisions, many suicides, and ghost stories — phantom vehicles plunging, lights beneath the water, and unexplained calls for help.

name: Tampa Theatre
content: The historic Tampa Theatre (opened 1926) hosts reports of a ghostly projectionist, eerie voices in the balcony, and footsteps in the old original projection booth long after sunset.

name: The Old Jail – St. Augustine
content: Built in 1891, the Old Jail in St. Augustine features hanging gallows, creaking cell doors, and reports of past inmates lingering in the dark corridors.

name: Vinoy Resort
content: Opened in 1925 in St. Petersburg, this grand resort is notorious among visiting MLB players who report seeing a towering phantom gentleman in a top hat, flickering lights, and moving furniture in upper rooms.

name: Wakulla Springs Lodge
content: Built in 1937 near Wakulla Springs, guests and staff report encounters with the gentle ghost of founder Edward Ball wandering the lodge's Mediterranean-style grand lobby and terrace.
